crime: Every evening until lockup, a girl who grew up sleeping round a mountain hut's stove naps by the lounge fireplace, letting {WITCH_NAME} sit by her and tap out her heartbeat.
One evening, as she drifts off, her heart quickens under {WITCH_NAME}'s ear. She takes the tapping hand: "You don't have to count my heart. I'm not going anywhere."

{WITCH_NAME} once lay counting with a hand on her mother's chest. Her mother, home only some nights, said: "You don't need to count. I'll be here." By morning her side of the bed was cold. Anyone who says that is already leaving.

At eight, hearing no other heart nearby, {WITCH_NAME} lays her ear on the sleeper's chest and presses a palm over her mouth and nose until the beat under her ear stops. She keeps tapping a slow, calm beat and feeds the fire. When the others return to cards, the girl's face is turned into her lap. For fun, they grip their own wrists as {WITCH_NAME} taps their pulses back, matching each beat, quickening with theirs.

At nine, a girl beats out an ember burning the sleeper's sleeve. The sleeper never stirs, and the tapping stays slow and calm; the girls laugh that she sleeps through anything. At nine-thirty, {WITCH_NAME} leaves her asleep and goes to the shower room with the others until lockup.
At ten to ten, the girl's roommate comes up to wake her and finds her not breathing, finger marks round her mouth, still warm from the fire.

In the trial court, the prisoners turn on the roommate: "She was smothered after nine-thirty, while {WITCH_NAME} was showering with us." One holds up the burned sleeve: "No sleeper lies still while fire eats through her sleeve, and no living heart stays calm under it." They realize she was dead before nine, and the girl who hears every heart sat tapping one that wasn't there.
fields.epitaph: The one heart that could never leave her was the one she had to pretend to hear.
fields.epithet: Counter of Hearts That Might Leave
execution: A rack of hearth logs rises above her where she lies strapped on her back. One at a time, the logs drop onto her chest on a slow, steady beat, and the pile grows heavier as her hands clench. The logs keep dropping onto the pile on the same slow beat, and her hands lie open and still.

magic.name: Every Heart a Clock
magic.text: She can hear the heartbeat of every person and animal around her.
